shortcut_name: naive exponential DFS treated as feasible because k is only 22
evidence: "dfs(m_idx)" iterates through every pathway for each base; "depth-first search" with three used-resource masks and no pruning
affordance_in_statement: The number of product batches required is k ... bounded ... by a maximum physical capacity of 22 batches. ... (1 ≤ k ≤ 22, 0 ≤ t ≤ k·k·k)
removal_suggestion: Do not imply that k=22 makes exhaustive search practical; instead present the instance as adversarial, with up to k^3 pathways and many partial selections surviving until deep in the search. This preserves the bounds while making the required worst-case behavior explicit.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Backtracks over bases in numeric order and accepts the first unused reagent/profile pair, with no memoization, matching-based pruning, or component reasoning.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The chosen subset must use every base compound, reagent, and thermal profile exactly once; k is at most 22.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a three-mask DFS over all pathways, assuming the 22-depth search is tractable despite potentially exponential branching.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The chosen subset must use every base compound, reagent, and thermal profile exactly once; k is at most 22.

common_affordance: the immutable small-looking bound k ≤ 22 encourages unpruned exponential backtracking over the exact three-resource matching constraints

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Enumerates every k-element subset of the t pathways using combinations, which is prohibitively expensive when t is as large as k^3.

Its shown reduction groups pathways by (m,c) into mc_to_f, which does not by itself enforce the global one-to-one use of all three resource dimensions; reducing a 3-dimensional matching instance to these pair buckets can reject valid instances or accept invalid ones.

recommended_edit: Add to the scenario that the pathway database may be adversarially ordered and may contain dense, deliberately ambiguous instances in which nearly all partial assignments remain viable until late in the search. This re-presents the immutable k≤22 bound as a worst-case exact-matching challenge and directs tests toward defeating fixed-order unpruned DFS.
